title: Apples, Red Delicious, with skin, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Red Delicious is one of the most popular apple varieties. It features a bright red skin, sweet‑tart flavor, and crisp texture. Apples are usually eaten raw but are also used in cooking, baking, and juicing.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Red Delicious cultivar was developed in the United States in the 1870s and quickly became a favorite for its taste and appearance.
Apple skin contains a high amount of antioxidants, especially polyphenols and quercetin.
Red Delicious is often showcased in fruit beauty contests because of its vivid color and uniform shape.
Apples can be stored for several months under proper conditions while retaining flavor and nutrients.
There are many ‘Delicious’ varieties, but Red Delicious is considered the sweetest.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Apples provide a good source of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber in apples improves digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Antioxidant content
items.content: Flavonoids and polyphenols in the skin protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Apple consumption is associated with lower LDL‑cholesterol levels.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A medium apple contains about 80 kcal, making it a convenient snack for weight management.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to apples, especially those with oral allergy syndrome.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: The skin can retain pesticide residues; it is advisable to wash apples thoroughly or choose organic varieties.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Excessive consumption may irritate the stomach in people with high acidity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Apples can be eaten whole, sliced into salads, added to oatmeal or yogurt, baked in pies, or juiced. Keeping the skin is recommended, as it holds most of the nutrients.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store apples in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer, in a perforated plastic bag. At room temperature they keep for 1‑2 weeks, and in the fridge up to 2 months.
